svg.text: ACTION CHUNK SEAM BOUNDARY: DERIVATIVE CONTINUITY VS. TRANSMISSION SHOCK
Systems Dynamics of Unchecked C⁰ Concatenation vs. Jerk-Continuous C² Quintic Spline Trajectory Blending
Chunk B arrives at t = 48 ms
CASE A: UNCHECKED C⁰ POSITION-ONLY CONCATENATION
CASE B: JERK-CONTINUOUS C² QUINTIC BLENDED SPLINE
SYSTEMS IMPLICATION: CONCATENATION REQUIRES HIGHER-ORDER BOUNDARY VALIDATION
When an action chunk finishes, splicing a replacement that matches only position (C⁰) creates an instantaneous velocity step Δq̇.
Across a 1.0 ms servo cycle (T_c), this step demands an acceleration impulse q̈ = Δq̇/T_c = 600 rad/s², transmitting 324 N·m through reflected inertia (J = 2.7 kg·m²) and shearing the drive pin.
